reason: Phagocytes are shown clearing debris at the cut, a likely first part of wound repair.
expectation: The wound will be cleared of some debris.

effect: The wound is cleared of debris and now has supply, surface and support slots to fill.
reaction: The named slots make the next stages clearer.
reason: Repair signals are shown acting on the nearby capillary, suggesting they can help establish the wound's supply.
expectation: The signals will stimulate a blood supply for the healing wound.

effect: The repair signals produced a capillary sprout connected to the existing circulation, suggesting it can fill the wound’s supply slot.
reaction: The connection to the parent vessel makes the new supply easy to follow.
reason: The capillary sprout appears to provide the supply needed by the healing skin.
expectation: The sprout will be fitted as the wound’s blood supply.

effect: The capillary sprout filled the supply slot and formed a connected route that can deliver nutrients to the wound.
reaction: The completed loop makes the supply’s purpose clear.
reason: Fibroblasts and matrix nutrients suggest a way to build the wound’s supporting tissue.
expectation: The fibroblasts will use the nutrients to make supporting matrix.

effect: Fibroblasts made new connective tissue, which appears suited to the wound’s support slot.
reaction: The collagen fibres make the supporting role clear.
reason: The new connective tissue can support the healing wound.
expectation: The connective tissue will fill the support slot.

effect: The new connective tissue filled the support slot; the result explains that this young tissue is still weaker than uninjured skin.
reaction: The distinction between closing the wound and regaining strength is useful.
reason: Epidermal edge cells and cell nutrients look like the pieces needed to rebuild the wound surface.
expectation: The edge cells will use the nutrients to form new surface tissue.

effect: The edge cells formed a new surface that can fill the remaining surface slot.
reaction: The sheet extending across the gap makes its role clear.
reason: The new surface should close the remaining gap in the healing skin.
expectation: The new surface will fill the surface slot and close the wound.

effect: The new surface closed the gap, completing the wound closure goal; the deeper tissue is still gaining strength.
reaction: The reminder that healing continues after closure is useful.
reason: Clot-clearing enzymes are shown breaking down fibrin, matching the remaining goal.
expectation: The enzymes will clear the temporary clot from the healing wound.

effect: The clot-clearing enzymes left a closed wound with a still-maturing scar, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The contrast between the temporary clot and the tissue that remains is satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the new connective tissue was most worthwhile: it showed how fibroblasts support the wound and explained that young tissue is still weaker than uninjured skin.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making and then fitting the new surface felt somewhat repetitive, though the picture of cells crossing the gap made the result clear.

surprise.text: The capillary sprout joined another vessel to form a local flow route; I had expected a supply but had not anticipated that detail.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. The named slots and picture descriptions gave each combination a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: connecting cellular actions to a healing wound was clear and interesting, even though several fitting steps were predictable.
